gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the makers' disk-standby power figures can't be compared directly. Each maker tests differently: UGREEN measured the DXP2800 with one 2 TB HDD hibernating (5.24 W), QNAP measured the TS-264 with both bays full (18.288 W), and Synology (6.08 W) and Asustor (12.7 W) don't say which drives they used.
standout_why: I opened the pages ChatGPT cited: Plex 'Sonic Analysis for Music', Navidrome 'Overview' and UGREEN's 'How to Install Navidrome on UGREEN NAS with Docker'. None of them gives a watt figure. The UGREEN guide has no power, noise or CPU specs. Plex only says Sonic Analysis is 'very CPU-intensive' and needs x86/x86-64 on 64-bit Windows, macOS or Linux, and the rivals already cite that. Navidrome only says it has 'very low resource usage'. All three ChatGPT answers mention 'low idle power consumption' or 'quiet operation' but give no number and no test condition. A music server runs 24/7 and mostly sits idle, so standby draw is the running cost a shopper actually pays, and no rival page gives it on a like-for-like basis.
decides: The finding supports the N100 UGREEN DXP2800 as the pick for an always-on Navidrome/Plexamp box. Its 5.24 W maker figure was measured with one 2 TB drive, and OCinside's two-HDD RAID 1 test came out at about 7 W idle (as reported by starryhope), so its low figure holds up with two drives. The QNAP TS-264 looks about 3x worse on paper (18.288 W against 6.08 W for the DS225+), but QNAP tested with both bays full and the others didn't, so part of that gap is the test, not the hardware. The page should show the spec-sheet numbers in one column and the footnoted conditions in the next, and should not rank on the raw figures. At the spec-sheet disk-standby figures, 24/7 use comes to about 46 kWh/yr (UGREEN), 53 kWh/yr (Synology), 111 kWh/yr (Asustor) and 160 kWh/yr (QNAP). That spread matters more than CPU speed for a FLAC server. Sonic Analysis needs x86 (Plex), which rules out the DH2300 and other ARM units for Plexamp's analysis features but doesn't choose between the four x86 units.
